posts.author: vforge
posts.content_md:
I'm thinking about building my own laser diode module from a raw diode. Does anybody know where to find the current 635nm to 640nm high power laser diodes with single mode? So far I have found an Opnext 635nm diode at up to 35mw, and a Sanyo 635-640nm diode at 40mw. The Sanyo costs over $ 390.00 and the Opnexts are about $ 170.00, but I suspect there are other options too. Mitsubishi, maybe.

I want to build my own module by affixing the diode to a peltier junction, and monitoring the temperature and the internal LD photodiode for power. I'm moderately handy with opamps and soldering irons and such, but does this sound like a realistic project? Has anybody else tried to make a long coherence length module out of bare laser diodes?

Any info would be much appreciated, and likewise I will share whatever I learn along the path to making one of these lasers.

Thanks.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
I worked on one for quite awhile before I gave up. I think I was on the right path but I really needed a good scope and mine was not very useful. You can see some of the work here:

[http://www.designerinlight.com/holo/laser.htm](http://www.designerinlight.com/holo/laser.htm)

I since sent some of the parts to a friend to see if he can have better results. We'll post if we have any success.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
Digikey has a Sharp 50 mW 654 nm diode (Sharp GH06550B2B), Digikey p/n 425-1807-ND for $74.03. I haven't tried it, but it's cheap enough so it's not a disaster if it's not suitable for holography. 

You may also want to look into getting a laser power meter - the topic has come up here several times. Because of part-to-part variation, it's very difficult to work with bare diodes unless you have a way to measure the output power.

Thanks for the advice!

As to the actual LD driver, I take it from the experiments that a constant current source is whats needed. Or do people use constant photodiode current? Whatever, I guess I am going to need a laser power meter. Off to ebay for that.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
A few helpful links:

[http://members.misty.com/don/laserdps.htm](http://members.misty.com/don/laserdps.htm) - Sam's the man!

[http://www.optima-optics.com/](http://www.optima-optics.com/) - laser diodes, mounts & optics

[http://users.bestweb.net/~hobbs/](http://users.bestweb.net/~hobbs/) - sample chapter contains helpful info on thermal control

[http://optics.ph.unimelb.edu.au/atomopt/diodes.html](http://optics.ph.unimelb.edu.au/atomopt/diodes.html) - mostly IR stuff, but applicable to visible diodes. Check out the refernces and search for "extended cavity diode laser" on Google for much more. Maybe overkill for holography, but interesting.

[http://www.ilxlightwave.com/appnotes/mo ... lasers.pdf](http://www.ilxlightwave.com/appnotes/mode_hopping_semiconductor_lasers.pdf)

The above is one of several very helpful notes from ILX:

[http://www.ilxlightwave.com/navpgs/tech_notes.html](http://www.ilxlightwave.com/navpgs/tech_notes.html)

I would also recommend browsing the archives of this forum.

Re constant current versus constant power - For holography I prefer constant current (actually I use constant voltage + resistor). This requires a thermally stabilized laser which can be done either actively via Peltier, or passively by coupling to a large thermal mass which is insulated from ambient temperature changes. I prefer the latter. The archives contain extensive discussions of this topic.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
I would strongly advise you to use constant current. Constant power only works when it settles into a constant current state. When a diode stops mode hopping it is constant current, constant power and a constant temperature. You must have all three things or it will mode hop.

I used a 4 amp TEC but it was way overkill. You could use a much smaller one. Also, it is very important to seperate the diode from the otherside of the TEC in a thermal sense. Please read the information at melcor.com if you don't have any experience with TECs.
